Wrote `objects-01-advanced.p01.verdicts.jsonl` — 150 lines, one per CSV row, in CSV order. I judged all 150 `sop` circuits myself; no other file in this folder was created or changed.

Result: 146 L8, 4 rejections.

| n | grade | reason |
|---|---|---|
| 33 | L2 | `not` in `not only for the diagram…` held in `discourse`, negation lost |
| 101 | L1 | `figure` in `make a woman figure my avatar` made the verb of a nonfinite clause, splitting the nominal and stripping the command's object |
| 165 | L2 | same `not`-in-`discourse` defect as n=33 |
| 349 | L3 | `my avatar` attached to the participle `painted` (`the robot but painted blue my avatar`) instead of being the complement of `make` |

Each rejection carries a corrected circuit I wrote in the rules' schema; I verified the four corrections parse, have unique wire ids, valid `$` references, and hold every word of their message exactly once.

The three wrong circuits are single-clause slips inside an otherwise repeated template — the rest of the packet is five near-identical message families whose circuits are consistent, which is why the rejections cluster on those three rows rather than spreading. Two judgement calls worth flagging: I accepted `conjunction="instead of"` in a coordination (n=54 and clones) and `"not only"` inside a coordination's conjunction (n=98, n=346), reading both as the word kept on a real tie rather than a misplaced negation; a stricter judge could call those L3 and L1.
